We want Pinpoint to be the best place you've ever worked, somewhere you feel valued, supported and excited to grow. Here's what you get:
  • Comprehensive healthcare: excellent medical, dental and vision coverage for you and your family
  • Unlimited holidays: take the time you need to rest and recharge
  • Mental health support: unlimited, immediate access to professional counselling via Spill
  • Retirement contributions: 401k or pension contributions depending on your location
  • Remote first: work where you're most productive, with flexibility and trust as the default
  • Equity with real upside: share in the long term value you help create
  • Fully paid parental leave: up to 16 weeks of paid leave for new parents
  • Learning budget: annual funds for courses, books or anything that supports your growth
A detailed overview of our benefits is here.

What you're wondering

  • Do I need to be a qualified lawyer? No. Contracts managers, legal ops leads and commercial managers are in scope if you've owned customer side contracts with real negotiation authority and done hands on GDPR work.
  • Who will I work with? You'll report to me and work closely with our Account Executives, Product and Engineering, and you'll decide what genuinely needs external counsel.
  • What tools will I use? We lean heavily on AI, Claude in particular, and we'd expect you to push it further in how legal works.
  • Where does the work come from? Mostly our sales team (about a third of the role), then data protection, product and partnerships. The split is shown in "What you'll do".
data.description:
Hi 👋 I'm the COO at Pinpoint.

We're a high growth HR tech company building software that helps in house recruitment teams attract, hire, and onboard the right talent. Today we have a strong foundation in place: a mature product, rapid growth, strong product market fit, and happy customers.

We've built strong operational foundations, but we've never had a dedicated lawyer. Legal work has been landing on the ops team, contract volume is up sharply, and the product is moving into even more regulated territory. We need someone to own legal end to end so our deals keep moving and our customers stay confident, which is why we're hiring a Founding Legal Counsel.

What you should know up front
  • This is a remote role based in the UK, with occasional in person team meetups.
  • You'll be our first dedicated legal hire, so you're building the function and inheriting the old contracts and processes at the same time.
  • You'll be the sole member of the legal team and will own both the judgment and the tactical work: marking up contracts, chasing signatures, building templates, and staying on top of compliance.
  • There's no one to delegate to, and there's no escalation for the day to day slog.
  • The volume is heavy, and the pace is fast. This role suits someone who likes to build and who's hands on; it's not a quiet compliance desk.
  • Our values actually matter here. We hire people who reflect them in how they work, collaborate, and make decisions.
data.key_responsibilities:
Sales legal (35%)
  • Own commercial contracting end to end: our MSA, DPA and customer red lines. You're who the Account Executives bring a marked up agreement to, and you're who closes it out
  • Turn around a high volume of reviews at pace. Contract volume is spiking, driven by growth and by the rise in AI usage
  • Set and publish a legal SLA for sales, so turnaround is a promise, not a guess
  • Own our risk tolerance and playbook: liability caps, indemnities, termination. Know where we flex, where we hold, and when to escalate
  • Run legal intake: what needs you, what sales can self serve, and what genuinely needs external counsel
  • Build the playbooks, fallback positions and templates that let AEs answer the easy questions without you
Data protection, governance and audit readiness (30%)
  • Own data protection across the business: our DPA, sub processor management, DPIAs, DSARs, records of processing and international transfers
  • Keep us on the right side of UK and EU GDPR, US state privacy law, and the local regimes that surface in deals (Quebec Law 25 and China's PIPL are recent examples)
  • Make audit readiness a habit, not a scramble, with policies that reflect what we actually do
  • Get us diligence ready: corporate housekeeping, share and option documentation, and cleaning up historic contractual exposure before someone else finds it
Product legal (20%)
  • Partner with Product and Engineering as we build in a regulated space: background screening, right to work, DBS and credit checks, and AI assisted hiring features
  • Own regulatory compliance as the landscape shifts: UK and EU GDPR, FCRA, the EU AI Act, and a growing patchwork of US state law
Partnerships, NDAs and supplier terms (15%)
  • Draft and negotiate partnership, reseller and referral agreements, including integration and marketplace partners
  • Own NDAs, supplier and vendor terms, and the contract lifecycle from template to signature to renewal
  • Keep supplier and integration partner terms robust and commercial
data.skills_knowledge_expertise:
• 4+ years as a qualified lawyer, or as a contracts manager, legal ops lead or commercial manager with real negotiation authority
  • A clear point of view on SaaS commercial terms (what's standard, what's risky, where to flex) from owning customer side contracts end to end: MSAs, order forms, DPAs, NDAs, red lines and liability caps
  • Hands on UK and EU GDPR experience: DPAs, DPIAs, DSARs, sub processors, records of processing and international transfers, done as a practitioner, not only from a policy seat
  • Time in a scaling company (roughly 30 to 250 people), with limited resources, shifting priorities and a lot of context switching
  • Breadth over narrow specialism: happy owning everything from a small order form to our data posture to exit readiness
  • A bias toward finding the defensible yes and containing the risk, rather than blocking deals and calling it caution
  • Comfort making the call: assess the ask, propose the route, and escalate only the genuine trade offs
  • Quick to pick up new tools, and comfortable pushing AI further in your work
  • Clear, concise communication that helps other teams move
  • Self motivated and happy working independently
You may not enjoy this role if
  • You'd rather advise than do the tactical work: marking up contracts, chasing signatures and building templates
  • You need every decision to have a precedent or sign off from above
  • Your background is mainly litigation, employment or pure IP, rather than commercial contracting
data.title: Founding Legal Counsel

Hi 👋 I'm Anna, Head of Implementation at Pinpoint.

We're a high growth, bootstrapped HR tech company building software that helps in house recruitment teams attract, hire, and onboard the right talent. More than 1,000 organisations use it, and if you read our reviews on G2 and Capterra you'll see how often customers mention the quality of our support and onboarding. That experience starts with implementation.

As we bring on more large, complex customers, we need someone to fully own a high volume of mid market and enterprise implementations from end to end, which is why we're hiring an Enterprise Implementation Manager. You'll steer timelines, manage technical complexity, and lead customers confidently through a high stakes rollout.

What you should know up front
  • This is a remote role based in the UK. Our HQ is in Jersey, and most of our team is UK based.
  • Initially you'll manage 8 to 12 active implementations, scaling to 15 to 20+ as you build efficiency. Most are mid market and enterprise projects, each running an average of 50 days.
  • Our product is deep, flexible, and genuinely complex. You'll work with customers running intricate, multi tenant workflows and customised hiring journeys, with a wide range of integration needs.
  • Pinpoint isn't for everyone. We're still in startup mode: fast moving, lean, and sometimes ambiguous. You'll thrive here if you're proactive, adaptable, and comfortable building structure where none exists.
  • Our values actually matter here. We hire people who reflect them in how they work, collaborate, and make decisions.
data.key_responsibilities:
• Get every implementation live on time, with deadlines met and blockers cleared with urgency
  • Own project management from kickoff through go live: milestones, risks, and keeping everyone aligned
  • Lead internal and external discovery, then design an implementation plan that fits each customer
  • Scope and shepherd HRIS integrations: read the API docs, map the data, and reduce engineering dependency where you can
  • Keep integrations, product and support moving together, with timely delivery and clear communication
  • Be a trusted advisor to enterprise customers on workflow design and product best practice
  • Hand customers over smoothly to Customer Success, and stay involved through early adoption
  • Build and deliver training that scales: live sessions, train the trainer programs, and self serve materials
data.skills_knowledge_expertise:
• 3+ years leading large B2B SaaS implementations end to end, across more than one product and with both enterprise and mid market customers
  • Experience running 10+ complex implementations at once, balancing competing priorities, internal coordination and technical complexity
  • Technical self sufficiency. You learn from API documentation, use tools like Postman to troubleshoot, and dig in rather than wait for engineering. You don't need to be a developer.
  • Time in high growth startups (roughly 50 to 250 people), where processes changed as the business scaled
  • A structured way of running projects: milestone driven plans, clear customer responsibilities, and thinking 2 to 3 steps ahead on risk
  • Real examples of managing implementation risk: changing the plan, unblocking a technical issue, or driving a change through
  • Operational rigour. People trust you to own outcomes, not just tasks.
  • AI in your day to day work. You actively use Claude, ChatGPT or similar for planning, research, communication and training materials.
  • Professional polish and presence. You can command a (virtual) room.
  • Bonus: HR or recruiting tech experience
You may not enjoy this role if
  • Your implementation experience has mostly been support, customer success or consultancy
  • You've only ever worked inside large, highly structured companies
  • You'd rather coordinate other people's work than own the outcome yourself
data.title: Enterprise Implementation Manager

A detailed overview of our benefits is here.

What you're wondering

  • What does success look like in the first 90 days? By 30 days you can answer a Support question about a stuck check without me. By 60 you own one of the Q4 items end to end with the plan written into Linear. By 90 I'm out of Marketplace standups and you're the named design owner on the Marketplace roadmap.
  • How does the design team actually use AI? Designers here ship real PRs, written with Claude against our product and design system repos and reviewed by an engineer like anyone else's. We prototype in code rather than Figma for anything complex, and we've built AI that checks AI: a design code review skill that runs before a PR, plus design system and token compliance checks.
    Claude still misses the last mile on padding, states and tokens, so human review is mandatory and nothing ships without it. 
  • Is there really no research function? No dedicated researcher, and there won't be one. There is a documented method set, discussion guide templates, and a live list of customers who have agreed to talk to us, with the intro coming warm from their CSM. What's been missing on Marketplace is the time to use it: for two quarters I've been the designer, the PM and the Head of Design at once. You'd have the access. We want someone who can make a good call fast, then pull the squad back toward research backed judgement as the default.
  • What tools do you use? Figma, Thumbtack (our design system in Figma and Storybook), Claude and Claude Code, Linear, Fibery, PostHog, Notion and Slack. The product is Rails and React with TypeScript.

Hi 👋 I'm Elvin, Head of Design at Pinpoint.

We're a high growth HR tech company building software that helps in house recruitment teams attract, hire, and onboard the right talent. Today we have a strong foundation in place: a mature product, rapid growth, strong product market fit, and happy customers.

Inside Pinpoint sits a part of the product most ATSs don't have: background checks, right to work, reference checks, one way video interviews and the credits and billing that power them. We call it Marketplace. It's the squad behind the revenue that scales with how much customers use us, and an important strategic bet towards continued growth.

For the past two quarters I've been its designer, its PM and the Head of Design at the same time. The next phase is harder than what we've already shipped, and it needs someone whose whole job it is, which is why we're hiring a Staff Product Designer.

You'll be the only designer on the Marketplace squad, working alongside our Head of Commercial Product (the squad's PM), our Tech Lead, a Senior Product Engineer, and our Head of Roadmap Engineering.

What you should know up front
  • 100% remote. You can be based in the UK, Portugal, Spain or Poland, working UK hours, with a few in person team meetups a year. We're headquartered in Jersey with a team of 100 across the UK, EU and US.
  • The product is a set of status driven workflows: a check gets ordered, a vendor or a regulator decides what happens next, and the design has to handle every outcome, including the ones that fail. Our third party vendors set what's possible and the compliance rules are fixed, so you'll spend as much time understanding how a vendor actually behaves as you do in Figma.
  • AI is how we work, not a tool we're trialling. I ship my own PRs through Claude Code now, and I hadn't shipped one 3 months ago. You don't need to have done that yet, but you do need to be using AI across your work today and to want to learn.
  • There's no dedicated researcher. Decisions have been quick and under pressure for a while. We want someone who can make a good call fast and who also pulls the squad toward research backed judgement as the norm.
  • Our values actually matter here. We hire people who reflect them in how they work, collaborate, and make decisions.
data.key_responsibilities:
• Own design for every usage based feature in Pinpoint, end to end: from the first conversation with a vendor or customer, through the spec and the design, to shipped and measured.
  • Ship the next phase of Pinpoint Checks: DBS update service with automated routing, rechecks, sending check data to downstream systems, decision and audit flows, and the UK high compliance checks that follow.
  • Turn credits from something customers are given into something they understand and use. Credit visibility, self serve costing and in platform credit management are being scoped now and they are yours to design.
  • Shape Marketplace product strategy with the PM going into 2027, then execute on it. Discovery here is shared between you and the PM, not handed to you.
  • Write the plan into the ticket before anything is built: the decisions made, the edge cases covered, the questions closed, so an engineer (or you) can build it with Claude without a second round of questions.
  • Prototype in code where it beats Figma, submit your own PRs for small front end fixes, and QA what ships.
  • Be the person Support, Sales and Legal come to when a check is stuck or a customer asks what a vendor does with their data. You'll know the domain better than almost anyone in the company within 90 days.
  • Bring Marketplace work to weekly design crit and feed new patterns (status cards, order flows, decision recording) back into Thumbtack, our design system.
data.skills_knowledge_expertise:
• Experience designing complex B2B software products alongside a PM and engineers, with shipped work to show for it. Owning an area as the sole or lead designer is a plus
  • Startup or scale up experience and the mentality that comes with it: small teams, few handoffs, and a willingness to do whatever the product needs that week
  • Hands on work designing around constraints set by someone else: a regulator, a compliance rule or a third party vendor's API. Background screening, identity, fintech, payments, insurance and legal are the obvious homes for it, and comparable complexity elsewhere counts
  • Multi state workflows in the portfolio, such as orders, cases, applications and checks, where the system decides the next step and the design has to handle the moments when it can't
  • Familiarity with what changes at enterprise scale: permissions, configuration, multiple personas, and flows that hold up at 10 users and at 10,000
  • Daily use of AI across the whole job rather than only to produce screens faster, covering research, testing, investigating bugs, prototyping and documenting, plus the technical depth and appetite to learn to ship small PRs with Claude Code
  • Production ready UI craft that clears a high bar, shown in the portfolio
  • Ownership of the call when the data isn't there: deciding, explaining the reasoning, owning the outcome, and solving the problem in front of you whether or not it is strictly a design problem. Over time, pulling the squad towards research backed judgement as the norm
  • Fluency in commercial outcomes, so margin, adoption and conversion get discussed as naturally as flows and components
  • Bonus points for HR tech or ATS experience, and for credits, billing or usage based pricing
You may not enjoy this role if
  • You want a research team, a brief and a backlog handed to you. Here you write the brief.
  • You're waiting to see how the AI thing plays out before changing how you work.
  • You'd rather own the design system or lead a team. This is an IC role on one squad, and Thumbtack governance stays with me.
  • Your portfolio is agency work or consumer apps only. Marketplace serves enterprise customers ordering checks at volume, and the panel will test for it.
data.title: Staff Product Designer
